record.paper_title: Report from the Open Problems Session at OPSFA13
record.original_question: Given a hypergeometric orthogonal polynomial family P_n(x; a) with parameters a and a connection relation expressing P_n(x; a) in another parameter family P_k(x; b), obtain closed-form expressions for the generalized linearization coefficients γ_{k,m,n}(a,b) in expansions of the form P_m(x; a)P_n(x; a) = Σ_{k=0}^{m+n} γ_{k,m,n}(a,b) P_k(x; b), ideally in hypergeometric closed form for families such as Gegenbauer and continuous q-ultraspherical/Rogers polynomials and, if possible, more broadly in the (q-)Askey scheme.

evidence.quote: Given a hypergeometric orthogonal polynomial Pn(x; a), where a is a set of arbitrary parameters, we would like to obtain closed-form expressions for the coeﬃcients of generalized linearization formulas.

The best chance for ﬁnding generalized linearization coeﬃcients which are hypergeometric functions is for the Gegenbauer and continuous q-ultraspherical/Rogers polynomials. This is because these linearization coeﬃcients are given by products of Pochhammer symbols. Perhaps other orthogonal polynomials in the (q-)Askey scheme are amenable to this calculation, but we have yet to uncover further closed-form linearization formulae.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{P_n(x;a)\}_{n\geq 0}$ denote a family of hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials depending on a tuple of parameters $a$ (for instance a family in the Askey scheme or its $q$-analogue, the $q$-Askey scheme). Suppose that for two parameter tuples $a$ and $b$ there is a known connection relation expressing $P_n(x;a)$ as a finite linear combination of $P_k(x;b)$. Define the generalized linearization coefficients $\gamma_{k,m,n}(a,b)$ by the expansion
$$P_m(x;a)\,P_n(x;a) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{m+n} \gamma_{k,m,n}(a,b)\, P_k(x;b).$$

Problem: Find closed-form expressions, ideally as (basic) hypergeometric series in the parameters and indices, for the coefficients $\gamma_{k,m,n}(a,b)$. In particular:

(a) Obtain such closed-form hypergeometric expressions for the Gegenbauer polynomials $C_n^{(\lambda)}(x)$ (with $a=\lambda$, $b=\mu$) and for the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) polynomials $C_n(x;\beta\,|\,q)$ (with $a=\beta$, $b=\gamma$).

(b) Determine, more broadly, for which other families in the Askey scheme and the $q$-Askey scheme the generalized linearization coefficients $\gamma_{k,m,n}(a,b)$ admit closed-form (basic) hypergeometric representations, and produce such representations where they exist.
artifact.status_search_result: Closed-form generalized linearization coefficients have been obtained for Gegenbauer and continuous q-ultraspherical/Rogers polynomials via connection relations and orthogonality (work by Cohl and collaborators), with specializations to continuous q-Hermite, continuous q-Legendre, Laguerre, and Chebyshev polynomials. Recent work (e.g., on two-dimensional contiguous relations for linearization coefficients of classical orthogonal polynomials, 2023) extends related computations, but a fully general closed-form treatment across the entire (q-)Askey scheme has not been achieved; the broader problem remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On a generalization of the Rogers generating function
status_evidence.snippet: A generalized Rogers generating function and corresponding definite integral for the continuous q-ultraspherical polynomials by applying its connection relation and utilizing orthogonality.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-form generalized linearization/expansion coefficients for continuous q-ultraspherical (Rogers) polynomials are obtained, with specializations to several subfamilies.

status_evidence.title: Two-dimensional contiguous relations for the linearization coefficients of classical orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Contiguous relations for linearization coefficients of classical orthogonal polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has produced structural relations for linearization coefficients of classical orthogonal polynomials, but not full closed-form formulas across the entire (q-)Askey scheme.

status_evidence.title: Linearization and Related Formulas for q-Ultraspherical Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Rogers' linearization formula for the q-ultraspherical polynomials whose coefficients completely factorize.
status_evidence.claim: Rogers' classical linearization formula provides the base case (a=b) with fully factorized coefficients.
